cohort: The participants were ~3-week-old mice, with 16 born by C-section and 23 by natural birth, under matched conditions.
finding: C-section did not inherently lead to large-scale shifts in gut microbiota populations in mice, but the abundance of Lachnoclostridium [Clostridium] scindens was significantly higher in C-section mice.
mod_finding: While C-section did not result in significant differences in alpha or beta diversity of gut microbiota, the abundance of Lachnoclostridium [Clostridium] scindens was significantly higher in mice born by C-section compared to natural birth.
